extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in functional analysis / PDEs
extracted.subtask_description: Statements, definitions, and criteria governing existence/uniqueness/regularity of solutions generated by (maximal) monotone or self-adjoint operators (Hille–Yosida theory), and the definition/ basic properties/embeddings/density/extension results for Sobolev spaces W^{1,p} in one dimension (variational formulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Density of D(A^2) in D(A) (Lemma 7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let u0 ∈ D(A). Then ∀ε > 0 ∃ u0' ∈ D(A^2) such that |u0' − u0| < ε and |A u0' − A u0| < ε. In other words, D(A^2) is dense in D(A) (for the graph norm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct u0' = J_λ u0 for small λ > 0; use properties of the resolvent J_λ and the fact J_λ A u0 = A J_λ u0. Choose λ small enough so J_λu0 approximates u0 in both u and Au.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness for initial data in D(A) (Theorem 7.4 / Step 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given u0 ∈ D(A) there exists a unique solution u of du/dt + A u = 0 on [0, ∞) with u ∈ C^1([0, ∞); H) ∩ C([0, ∞); D(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximate u0 by sequence in D(A^2), construct solutions for approximations, pass to the limit using uniform convergence and closedness of A; uniqueness arises from monotonicity (or energy estimates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of Yosida approximations (Remark 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If u0 ∈ D(A), then u_λ(t) converges as λ → 0 to u(t) ∈ C^1([0,∞);H) ∩ C([0,∞);D(A)) solving (6). (b) If u0 ∈ H only, u_λ(t) still converges pointwise to u(t) but the limit may not lie in D(A) for t>0 and may be nowhere differentiable—i.e., no classical solution for some u0 ∈ H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret u(t) as a generalized solution when u0 ∈ H; observe this pathology does not occur when A is self-adjoint (then u(t) is classical for every u0 ∈ H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contraction semigroup properties (Remark 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For SA(t) defined by the solution map u0 ↦ u(t): (a) SA(t) ∈ L(H) and ||SA(t)||_{L(H)} ≤ 1 for each t ≥ 0; (b) SA(t1 + t2) = SA(t1) ∘ SA(t2) ∀t1,t2 ≥ 0; (c) SA(0) = I and lim_{t→0+} ||SA(t)u0 − u0|| = 0 for all u0 ∈ H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These properties define a continuous semigroup of contractions. Because D(A) is dense in H and ||u(t)|| ≤ ||u0||, SA(t) extends by continuity to all H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bijective correspondence (Hille–Yosida remark)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a bijective correspondence between maximal monotone operators A and continuous semigroups of contractions S(t) on H: for each S(t) there exists a unique maximal monotone operator A with S(t)=S_A(t) ∀t ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the qualitative content of the Hille–Yosida theorem in the context of maximal monotone operators on a Hilbert space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift/trick for adding λu (Remark 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: To study du/dt + A u + λ u = 0 replace u by v(t)=e^{λ t} u(t), which reduces the problem to the original form dv/dt + A v = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This device allows handling spectral shifts or adding a damping/growth term by conjugation with exponential factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of D(A^k) and scalar product on D(A^k) (Section 7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inductively define D(A^k) = { v ∈ D(A^{k-1}); A v ∈ D(A^{k-1}) } for k≥2. Equip D(A^k) with scalar product (u,v)_{D(A^k)} = Σ_{j=0}^k (A^j u, A^j v) (and corresponding norm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D(A^k) is then a Hilbert space with this graph-type norm; used to bootstrap regularity by treating A as an operator on these spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher regularity: if u0 ∈ D(A^k) then u has higher regularity (Theorem 7.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume u0 ∈ D(A^k) for integer k ≥ 2. Then the solution u satisfies u ∈ C^{k−j}([0, ∞); D(A^j)) for all j=0,1,...,k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by induction: treat A as operator on H1=D(A) with domain D(A^2) etc.; use Theorem 7.4 applied to A_1, and bootstrap differentiability using that A maps H1→H and the equation du/dt + A u = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: symmetric and self-adjoint operators (Section 7.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A is symmetric if (A u, v) = (u, A v) ∀u,v ∈ D(A). A is self-adjoint if D(A^*) = D(A) and A^* = A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For bounded operators symmetric ⇔ self-adjoint. For unbounded operators symmetry does not imply self-adjointness; extra domain equality is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal monotone symmetric ⇒ self-adjoint (Proposition 7.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is maximal monotone and symmetric then A is self-adjoint (i.e., D(A^*) = D(A) and A^* = A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses J_1 = (I + A)^{-1}, showing J_1 self-adjoint and using representation arguments to show any u∈D(A^*) actually lies in D(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-adjoint case: existence/regularity for all u0 ∈ H (Theorem 7.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be self-adjoint maximal monotone. Then for every u0 ∈ H there exists unique u ∈ C([0, ∞); H) ∩ C^1((0, ∞); H) ∩ C((0, ∞); D(A)) solving du/dt + A u = 0 on (0, ∞). Moreover ||u(t)|| ≤ ||u0|| and ||du/dt(t)|| = ||A u(t)|| ≤ (1/t) ||u0|| for t>0; and u is smooth on (0,∞) with values in D(A^∞) (C^k((0,∞); D(A^∞)) for all k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness via monotonicity producing nonincreasing squared distance; existence by approximations (Yosida regularization u_λ), energy estimates yield bounds like ||du_λ/dt(T)|| ≤ (1/T)||u0|| (inequality (33)), then pass to limit λ→0. For u0∈H use density of D(A^2) and limiting arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate for Yosida approximations derivative (inequality (33))
rubrics_metrics.description: For u_λ solving du_λ/dt + A_λ u_λ = 0 with u_λ(0)=u0, one has ||du_λ/dt(T)|| ≤ (1/T) ||u0|| for all T>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive by multiplying equation by u_λ and by t du_λ/dt, integrating, using monotonicity properties, integration by parts and nonincreasing nature of t ↦ ||du_λ/dt(t)||.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hille–Yosida in Banach spaces and m-accretive operators (Theorem 7.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Banach space E, A is m-accretive if D(A)=E and (I + λ A) is bijective with ||(I + λ A)^{-1}|| ≤ 1 for all λ>0. If A is m-accretive then for any u0 ∈ D(A) there exists a unique u ∈ C^1([0,∞);E) ∩ C([0,∞); D(A)) solving du/dt + A u = 0, with ||u(t)|| ≤ ||u0|| and similar monotonicity of ||A u(t)||.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map u0↦u(t) extends to a contraction semigroup on E. Conversely, every continuous contraction semigroup corresponds to a unique m-accretive generator A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exponential formula (time-discretization limit) (Theorem 7.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is m-accretive then solution u(t) = lim_{n→∞} (I + (t/n) A)^{-n} u0 (the exponential formula).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: implicit time discretization (backward Euler) un = (I + (t/n)A)^{-n} u0 with time-step t/n; as n→∞ the discrete time-advance converges to the continuous semigroup S_A(t).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inhomogeneous equation solution formula (Theorem 7.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume A m-accretive. For u0 ∈ D(A) and f ∈ C^1([0,T];E) there exists unique u ∈ C^1([0,T];E) ∩ C([0,T];D(A)) solving du/dt + A u = f with u(0)=u0, and u(t)=S_A(t) u0 + ∫_0^t S_A(t−s) f(s) ds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If f ∈ L^1 the formula still defines a generalized solution; semigroup convolution yields Duhamel's formula. Extensions to semilinear equations du/dt + A u = F(u) are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variational program for boundary value problems (Step A–D, Chapter 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program outline: Step A define weak solution via Sobolev spaces; Step B obtain existence/uniqueness of weak solution by variational methods (Lax–Milgram); Step C prove regularity (weak→classical); Step D recover classical solution when weak solution is C^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the road-map for solving elliptic boundary value problems via variational methods; example given for −u''+u=f with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on [a,b].

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Sobolev space W^{1,p}(I) (Section 8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: W^{1,p}(I) = { u ∈ L^p(I); ∃ g ∈ L^p(I) such that ∫_I u φ' = −∫_I g φ ∀ φ ∈ C_c^1(I) }. Denote u' = g (distributional derivative). H^1(I)=W^{1,2}(I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to: u has distributional derivative in L^p. If u ∈ C^1 then classical derivative coincides with distributional one. Norms: ||u||_{W^{1,p}} = ||u||_{L^p} + ||u'||_{L^p} (or the p-norm variant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic functional-analytic properties of W^{1,p} (Proposition 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: W^{1,p} is a Banach space for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞; reflexive for 1<p<∞; separable for 1 ≤ p <∞. H^1 is a separable Hilbert space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via isometry T:W^{1,p}→L^p×L^p sending u↦(u,u'), closedness and standard Banach-space facts. Useful density/compactness consequences follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous representative and fundamental theorem (Theorem 8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If u ∈ W^{1,p}(I) (1 ≤ p ≤ ∞) then u has a continuous representative  (on closure ŌI) and for all x,y ∈ ŌI, (x) − (y) = ∫_y^x u'(t) dt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus each Sobolev class has a unique continuous representative; when convenient one replaces u by that representative. This yields pointwise meaning of u(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization via distributional testing (Proposition 8.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 1<p≤∞, u ∈ L^p belongs to W^{1,p} iff there exists C such that |∫_I u φ'| ≤ C ||φ||_{L^{p'}} for all φ ∈ C_c^1(I). One can take C = ||u'||_{L^p}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalence follows from extending the bounded linear functional to all of L^{p'} and representing it by g∈L^p (Riesz). For p=1 the implication one way holds but converse fails (BV vs AC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolutely continuous vs bounded variation remark (Remark 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: On bounded I: W^{1,1}(I) equals absolutely continuous functions (AC) characterized by small total oscillation on small total measure; functions satisfying the testing inequality with p=1 are functions of bounded variation (BV). BV functions need not have continuous representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish AC (integration of L^1 derivative and continuity) from BV (distributional derivative a bounded measure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of W^{1,∞} as Lipschitz functions (Proposition 8.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: u ∈ L^∞(I) belongs to W^{1,∞}(I) iff there exists C with |u(x) − u(y)| ≤ C |x − y| for a.e. x,y ∈ I. Moreover ||u'||_{L^∞} acts as the Lipschitz constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One direction from Theorem 8.2; the converse via difference quotient control and testing against φ ∈ C_c^1 to verify the distributional derivative is bounded (use Proposition 8.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation characterization on R (Proposition 8.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For u ∈ L^p(R) (1<p<∞), u ∈ W^{1,p}(R) iff there exists C such that for all h∈R, ||τ_h u − u||_{L^p} ≤ C |h|. One can take C = ||u'||_{L^p}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for checking W^{1,p} via difference estimates. The proof uses Theorem 8.2 for the forward implication and testing against φ for the reverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension operator for W^{1,p}(I) (Theorem 8.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists bounded linear P: W^{1,p}(I) → W^{1,p}(R) with P u|_I = u and ||P u||_{L^p(R)} ≤ C ||u||_{L^p(I)}, ||P u||_{W^{1,p}(R)} ≤ C ||u||_{W^{1,p}(I)}, where C depends only on |I|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction by reflection for half-line, and using cutoff and reflection about endpoints for bounded intervals. Constants are explicit up to universal factors; ensures operations like convolution/Fourier on extended functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Density of C_c^∞ approximations (Theorem 8.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For u ∈ W^{1,p}(I), 1 ≤ p < ∞, there exists a sequence u_n ∈ C_c^∞(R) with u_n|_I → u in W^{1,p}(I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: extend u to R (Theorem 8.6), mollify (convolution with mollifiers) and cut off (ζ_n) to obtain compactly supported smooth approximants; use convolution-differentiation commutation Lemma and dominated convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convolution preserves W^{1,p} and commutes with derivative (Lemma 8.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ρ ∈ L^1(R) and v ∈ W^{1,p}(R) then ρ * v ∈ W^{1,p}(R) and (ρ * v)' = ρ * v'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First prove for compact-support ρ using integration by parts; extend to general ρ by approximating with compactly supported ρ_n in L^1 and passing to the limit; used in density arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sobolev embedding in 1D and compactness (Theorem 8.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists C (depending only on |I|) with ||u||_{L^∞(I)} ≤ C ||u||_{W^{1,p}(I)} for all 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞; further, if I bounded then the injection W^{1,p}(I) ↪ C(ŌI) is compact for 1<p≤∞, and W^{1,1}(I) ↪ L^q(I) is compact for all 1≤q<∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives uniform (continuous) embedding of W^{1,p} into L^∞ in one dimension and Rellich-type compact embeddings on bounded intervals; fundamental tool for variational methods and passage to limits.
